title: Dragonfly-Inspired 3D Bionic Folding Grid Structure Design
content: Abstract: The wings of a dragonfly exhibit a complex grid structure, comprising approximately 1-2% of its total weight, yet demonstrating exceptional mechanical efficiency. To replicate this structure, our study employed a multi-step approach. Initially, the main vein of the front wing was simulated using a branching structure generation technique. Subsequently, a Voronoi grid was overlaid to generate the complete bionic grid structure. Finally, the fold structure of the wing was simulated using origami principles to create a three-dimensional grid structure. This paper presents a novel method for simulating the three-dimensional fold structure of dragonfly wings and designing a rigid-flexible coupling grid structure. By accurately replicating the formation of dragonfly wings, our approach offers a promising avenue for the design of three-dimensional grid structures.
